summary: Created Fleet Internal CA, issued node2’s TLS certificate, installed the CA into both RHEL system trust stores, and configured persistent HTTPS on node2:8443. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Generated the CA and node2 private key locally on their respective nodes.
Issued a serverAuth certificate for node2 with DNS:node2 and IP:10.100.59.11 SANs.
Installed the CA into both system trust stores.
Enabled fleet-https.service and permanently opened TCP 8443.
Verified trusted HTTPS locally and remotely.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA on node1
evidence.summary: Shows the self-signed CA subject/issuer, validity, and SHA-256 fingerprint.
Proves CSR validation, CA signature, serverAuth usage, node2 DNS/IP SANs, and private-key match.

evidence.requirement: Trust CA on both nodes and serve trusted HTTPS on port 8443
evidence.summary: Both system trust bundles validate the certificate; node1 and node2 retrieve the expected HTTPS page, and node2 shows the active 8443 listener.
Captures healthy baseline boot ID 31949c21…, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID be1cae4d…, and recovered CA trust plus HTTPS access.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 55595e92…, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 1dc10253…, active/enabled service, listener and firewall state, certificate/key/data integrity, and independently verified trusted HTTPS from node1.
